title: Shreyas Iyer Makes ODI Captaincy Debut as India Eye Series Seal
excerpt: Iyer leads India for the first time in the fourth ODI at Bay Oval on Friday, November 13, with the visitors 2-0 up after the Hamilton washout and one win away from sealing the series.
body:
• Fourth ODI: India vs New Zealand on Friday, November 13 at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui, starting 7:30 AM IST, live on Sony Sports Network and streaming on Sony LIV.
  • India lead the five-match series 2-0 after wins in Auckland and Wellington, with the third ODI in Hamilton washed out without a ball bowled; a win seals the series 3-0 with a match to spare.
  • Shreyas Iyer captains India in ODIs for the first time, with Shubman Gill and KL Rahul having moved into Test preparations and Ishan Kishan named vice-captain.
  • New Zealand are also reshuffled: several players have left for Test preparations, Lockie Ferguson is out with a calf injury, and uncapped Brett Randell has earned a maiden call-up.

Shreyas Iyer will begin his stint as India's ODI captain in the absence of regular skipper Shubman Gill when the visitors take on New Zealand in the fourth match of the five-game series at Bay Oval on Friday, IANS reported. It is a preview, not a formality: India hold a 2-0 advantage, and a victory would give them the series with a match to spare, while New Zealand need to win both remaining games to draw the series.

A new captain, with a point to prove

Gill and wicketkeeper-batter KL Rahul have moved into Test preparations, leaving Iyer to lead a squad that includes Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli. According to ANI's preview carried by NewKerala, Gill has been rested for the final two ODIs, along with Rahul, as part of a pre-planned workload management decision ahead of the two-match Test series against New Zealand beginning November 19, and the decision is not related to an injury. Iyer served as Gill's deputy in the first three matches.

The captaincy is only part of Iyer's test. PTI's preview, the basis of The Hindu's report, noted that Iyer will have a point to prove with the bat on his ODI captaincy debut and that his issues against the short ball have resurfaced in the series. Ishan Kishan has been named vice-captain and is among the wicketkeeping options, while Ruturaj Gaikwad, Tilak Varma, Naman Dhir and others give the team management different combinations to consider, IANS reported.

How the series has gone

India's two victories have come in rain-affected matches. Kohli's 74 set up the opening win in Auckland, while the bowlers took centre stage in Wellington, where Gurnoor Brar claimed four wickets as New Zealand were dismissed for 134, according to IANS. ANI's account added that in Auckland the hosts were bowled out for 185, with Arshdeep Singh taking four wickets, and India chased a revised target of 143 in 22.4 overs for a five-wicket win; in Wellington, India reached 113 for seven in 26 overs, surpassing a revised target of 110 under the DLS method. The third ODI in Hamilton was washed out without a ball being bowled.

There is also a personal milestone in view. ANI reported that Kohli is 22 runs away from becoming the first batter to score 2,000 runs against New Zealand in ODIs.

Team news on both sides

New Zealand are dealing with changes on several fronts. Tom Latham, Daryl Mitchell, Henry Nicholls, Glenn Phillips and Nathan Smith have left to prepare for the Test series, while Lockie Ferguson is unavailable with a calf injury, IANS reported. Blair Tickner is also ruled out of the fourth ODI under the mandatory stand-down period after being replaced due to concussion in the second match. Matt Henry is expected to return, Finn Allen is part of the squad for the final two games, and uncapped fast bowler Brett Randell has earned a maiden call-up and is likely to make his international debut.

For Mitchell Santner's side, IANS said the challenge is to rebuild the batting around Will Young, Tim Seifert, Nick Kelly and Allen, while Jacob Duffy, Kyle Jamieson and Henry shoulder the bowling responsibility. The final two ODIs also offer opportunities for India's Auqib Nabi and Yash Thakur to press their case.

How to watch

The fourth ODI is on Friday, November 13 at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui, starting at 7:30 AM IST. IANS reported the match will be shown live on the Sony Sports Network channels on TV, with live streaming available on the Sony LIV app and website. Bay Oval, IANS noted, offers batters a chance to settle once new-ball movement eases, although seamers can remain influential early on, so a complete 50-over contest would be a different test for both reshaped sides after a series shaped so far by rain.
